description: BatchNorm backward (spatial mode, saved mean and inverse variance from the forward pass) in the HIP_MLOPS_ENGINE region: rank 4 or 5, NCHW/NCDHW or NHWC/NDHWC strides, float/half/bfloat16 x, dy and dx with float scale, dscale, dbias and statistics (the backward kernels use a single fp_type for x, dy and dx, BatchNormBwdSpatial.cpp:837-839, although the applicability check would accept differing io dtypes, BatchnormApplicabilityChecks.cpp:65-76), N*H*W > 1, hw and n swept around the kernel-variant thresholds (hw 60/200/512/1024/4096, n 32/64/768) and powers of two +-1. Template: quick BatchnormBackward/Variant2 (saved mean and inv-variance, the full backward tensor set; Default recomputes the statistics and sets no mean/inv-variance). The tuned input ranges of the quick sweep are copied: inv_variance 1.9..2.0 stays positive, as an rsqrt output must. The axis domain (default/narrow/wide/positive/constant/nonzero/zeros/large/subnormal/nan/inf) renders the fills of x (uid 7) and dy (uid 3) in metadata.inputs; default keeps the quick sweep's x -1..1 and dy -0.1..0.1, the other finite domains use the shared table for both; large keeps scale 32 (worst-case half dx stays near 1e4, below 65504, because scale*inv_variance <= 0.2); scale, mean and inv_variance keep their tuned literal ranges. For nan and inf, x and dy stay at their default ranges (a non-finite x or dy element spreads through the channel sums to all of dscale, dbias and dx of its channel) and the special fill (5% of elements, at least one) goes on scale (uid 6): it only multiplies dx, so dscale and dbias stay finite and only the poisoned channels of dx are non-finite; c == 1 makes all of dx non-finite, which fails under match_nonfinite by design. The validator is match_nonfinite exactly for nan and inf. The last axes, alignment (1..256) and placement (default/exact/under), declare that alignment on every device tensor (tensor_patches on uids 0-7) and place the run's pointers accordingly; under misaligns x (placement_uid 7) and needs alignment >= 2, so eff_placement turns under into exact at alignment 1.

derive.d: ds if ndim == 5 and (hw // h) % ds == 0 else 1
derive.dims_x: [n, c, h, w] if ndim == 4 else [n, c, d, h, w]
derive.xs_h: w if layout == 'nchw' else w * c
derive.xs_d: h * w if layout == 'nchw' else h * w * c
derive.xs_c: d * h * w if layout == 'nchw' else 1
derive.stride_x: [xs_n, xs_c, xs_h, xs_w] if ndim == 4 else [xs_n, xs_c, xs_d, xs_h, xs_w]
derive.stride_s: [c, 1, ss_w, ss_w] if ndim == 4 else [c, 1, ss_w, ss_w, ss_w]
derive.dom_kind: 'fixed' if domain == 'constant' else 'nonzero' if domain == 'nonzero' else 'zeros' if domain == 'zeros' else 'large' if domain == 'large' else 'subnormal' if domain == 'subnormal' else 'free'
derive.dom_lo: -0.01 if domain == 'narrow' else -8.0 if domain == 'wide' else 0.25 if domain == 'positive' else 0.5 if domain == 'constant' else -1.0
derive.dom_hi: 0.01 if domain == 'narrow' else 8.0 if domain == 'wide' else 4.0 if domain == 'positive' else 0.5 if domain == 'constant' else 1.0
derive.eff_placement: 'exact' if placement == 'under' and alignment < 2 else placement

constraints.reason: backward is a training-mode op, so N * spatial must be > 1 (frontend validateBatchNormTrainingSpatialDimensions via BatchnormBackwardNode.hpp:162; engine BatchnormValidator::checkBwdTensorConfigSupported passes isTraining=true to validateSpatialDimensions, BatchnormApplicabilityChecks.cpp:29,414-437)

oracle cost ceiling (RFC 0023 section 14), lower than the 2**30 normalization ceiling because the GPU graph executor has no BatchNorm backward plan (GpuReferenceGraphExecutor.hpp:189), so the scalar CPU reference (CpuFpReferenceBatchnorm.hpp:296-394, three passes per channel with an index vector per element) is the oracle; keeps the extents inside the kernel's int template parameters too (Configuration.hpp proto_config, BatchnormBwdPlan.cpp:248-253)
